locator.section: 8 Detailed Mechanisms of Ion Fragmentation (Eq. 8.47, EE+ loss of NH3 from a protonated diamine)

evidence.curator_note: Anchimeric (neighbouring-group) displacement in the protonated 1,4-diaminobutane [M+H]+ (H2N(CH2)4N(+)H3): the neutral amine N1 lone pair attacks the terminal carbon C5 that bears the ammonium, forming the new N1-C5 bond and closing a five-membered ring, while the C5-N6 bond breaks heterolytically to expel neutral NH3. Charge migrates from N6 to N1; the product is the protonated pyrrolidine (pyrrolidinium) ion, drawn as the H2N(+) pentagon. Book draws 2 arcs; both encoded moves are drawn: move<1> (N1 lone pair -> new N1-C5 bond) and move<2> (C5-N6 bonding pair -> N6) are the two double-barbed curved arrows shown on the page. n=4 is highlighted as the sterically favourable case giving maximum NH3 loss (Audier et al. 1978). Validator soft notes 'lone pair rather than radicals' on atoms 1 and 6 are expected (both moves shuttle 2-electron lone pairs, not radicals).

locator.section: rule_index.json by_equation has no entry for 8.47

evidence.curator_note: No MØD rule is cross-linked: rule_index.json has no by_equation entry for 8.47. No m/z or abundance is printed for this scheme on the page, so the pyrrolidinium ion is detected=false with peak status 'inferred'; observed_mz 72.0802 is the curator-computed monoisotopic value for C4H10N+ (electron mass subtracted), NOT a measured value. The page names no ionization method: the precursor is treated as a protonated molecule [M+H]+ (m/z 89.1068 for C4H13N2+); ionization_method is set to CI as the canonical origin of an even-electron [M+H]+, but the page does not state it.
